content.title: Compress PDF File Size Free on iPhone and iPad
content.meta_description: Learn how to compress large PDF files on your iPhone or iPad for free. Reduce PDF size to meet email limits with a live preview of the final file size.
content.h1: How to Compress PDF File Size Free on iPhone and iPad
content.quick_answer: You can compress a PDF file for free on your iPhone or iPad using the Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit app. Select your PDF, choose the 'Compress PDF' option, and pick from three presets (High quality, Balanced, Smallest). The app shows a preview of the resulting file size before you save, helping you achieve your desired size for sharing.
intro: Sending a large PDF from your iPhone or iPad can be difficult. Email providers often reject attachments over 20-25 MB. This means your scanned contracts, reports, or tax forms might bounce back.

This page explains how to reduce your PDF's file size quickly and for free, ensuring it can be shared via email or other services. You will learn how to compress PDFs on-device, without uploading your documents to external servers.
We will cover the steps using Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit, an app that lets you choose compression levels and preview the final size before saving.
content.steps_heading: Compress a PDF on Your iPhone with Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit

steps.title: Open Your PDF in the App
steps.detail: Launch Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit. If your PDF is already in the app, tap to open it. If it is in Files or another app, use the Share Sheet to open it with Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit.

steps.title: Access the Compression Tool
steps.detail: With your PDF open, look for the option to compress. This will open the PDF compression screen.

steps.title: Choose a Compression Preset
steps.detail: The app offers three compression presets: High quality, Balanced, and Smallest. Each preset adjusts the image quality and compression level to reduce the file size. Select the option that best fits your needs.

steps.title: Preview the Resulting Size
steps.detail: After selecting a preset, the app displays a preview of the new, compressed file size. This lets you see the impact of your choice before committing. Adjust the preset if the file is still too large or if the quality loss is too high.

steps.title: Save or Share Your Compressed PDF
steps.detail: Once you are satisfied with the new size and quality, tap to save the compressed PDF. You can save it as a new file, or share it directly via AirDrop, Mail, or save to iCloud Drive, Google Drive, or Dropbox.

content.alternatives_heading: Other Ways to Reduce PDF File Size

alternatives.method: Built-in iOS Tools (Files or Notes app)
alternatives.how: The iOS Files app allows you to select several images or PDFs and choose 'Create PDF' to combine them. The Notes app also scans documents into PDFs. However, neither app offers a specific control for compressing a PDF to a target size.
alternatives.best_for: Creating basic PDFs from existing files or scanning single documents quickly.
alternatives.limitation: iOS has no built-in control for compressing a PDF to a target size. You cannot reduce an existing PDF's file size with these tools.

alternatives.how: Many websites offer free PDF compression. You upload your PDF to their server, and they return a compressed version.
alternatives.best_for: Occasional compression when you do not want to install an app.
alternatives.limitation: These tools require uploading your document to a third-party server. This can be a privacy concern for sensitive information like IDs, contracts, or financial records. Free tiers often limit file size or daily use.

alternatives.how: You can upload a PDF to Google Drive, then choose 'Open with > Google Docs'. This converts the PDF into an editable Google Docs document.
alternatives.best_for: Extracting text from a PDF to edit it, rather than simply reducing the PDF's size.
alternatives.limitation: This method converts the document to a new format, often losing original formatting. It is not designed for reducing the PDF file size while keeping it as a PDF.

content.features_heading: Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit Features for PDF Compression

feature_points.benefit: Reduce PDF file size with three presets (High quality, Balanced, Smallest) and preview the resulting size. This helps you meet email attachment limits without guesswork.
All compression runs on your iPhone or iPad. Your documents are processed locally and not uploaded to any server, ensuring privacy for sensitive files.
After compression, easily share your PDF via AirDrop, Mail, or save it directly to iCloud Drive, Google Drive, and Dropbox. This ensures your smaller file reaches its destination.

tips: Understand email attachment limits. Most email providers cap attachments at 20-25 MB. Aim for a file size below this threshold.
Choose the 'Balanced' preset first. It often provides a good balance between file size reduction and visual quality. Only go 'Smallest' if the file is still too large.
Always preview the resulting file size. The app shows you the new size before you save, so you can adjust your compression preset if needed.
Keep the original file. If quality is critical, save the compressed PDF as a new file, preserving your original high-quality document.

faqs.question: How do you compress a large PDF on iPhone without paying a subscription?
faqs.answer: You can compress a large PDF on your iPhone for free using Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit. The app's PDF compression feature is free to use. You can select your PDF, choose a compression level, and save the smaller file without any cost.

faqs.question: What are the compression presets and how do you preview the final size before saving?
faqs.answer: Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit offers three compression presets: High quality, Balanced, and Smallest. After you select a preset, the app displays a preview of the resulting file size. This allows you to see how much the PDF will shrink before you save it.

faqs.question: Does iOS have a built-in compression control inside Files or Notes?
faqs.answer: No, iOS does not have a built-in control for compressing a PDF to a specific target size within the Files or Notes apps. While these apps can create PDFs, they do not offer options to reduce the file size of an existing PDF.

faqs.question: Why do email providers reject large PDF attachments?
faqs.answer: Email providers reject large PDF attachments because they typically have file size limits, commonly around 20-25 MB per email. These limits help manage server load and ensure faster email delivery for all users.

faqs.question: Is on-device compression safer for confidential contracts and tax forms than online web tools?
faqs.answer: Yes, on-device compression is safer for confidential documents. Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit processes your files entirely on your iPhone, meaning your contracts, tax forms, or IDs are not uploaded to any third-party server. Online converters, by contrast, require you to upload your document, which can pose privacy risks.
